name: stage-0-en
text: Li Bai invites you to wander. Sing of the perilous roads of Shu, and the splendour of a sea of clouds. Across two poems, follow a journey from uncertainty to hope.

name: stage-1-en
text: Push open the doors. Wine and delicacies await, but the road in the poet’s heart is still uncertain.

name: stage-2-en
text: Fine wine in golden cups costs ten thousand a measure; rare food on jade plates is worth a fortune. Raise the cup, lower it gently, and taste a morsel. This brief banquet prelude makes the coming hesitation more poignant.

name: stage-3-en
text: I set down my cup and cast aside my chopsticks; I cannot eat. The hand hesitates before the food reaches the mouth. No further bite is taken. These interrupted gestures make sorrow visible.

name: stage-4-en
text: I draw my sword and look around, my heart bewildered. The blade is drawn; where does the road lead?

name: stage-5-en
text: Outside the feast, the city offers no answer. The poet’s bewilderment now unfolds into images of frozen rivers and mountains buried in snow.

name: stage-6-en
text: I would cross the Yellow River, but ice blocks its waters. The wish to advance meets a barrier. Look down at the broken layers of ice: the river becomes an image of a life obstructed.

name: stage-7-en
text: I would climb the Taihang Mountains, but snow fills their heights. The river is frozen; the mountain road is buried. The repeated contrast between intention and obstacle deepens the sense of frustration.

name: stage-8-en
text: Hard is the road! So many turnings, where is the way? The short phrases sound like urgent questions. We now turn to The Hard Road to Shu, where difficulty takes the form of an immense mountain landscape.

name: stage-9-en
text: Ah, how perilous, how high! The road to Shu is harder than climbing to the blue sky. The exclamation and exaggeration place human smallness against towering mountains.

name: stage-10-en
text: The earth split and mountains crumbled; the strong men died. Then skyward stairs and cliff paths were joined. An ancient legend evokes the immense cost of opening the road. Follow the connected stonework around the mountain.

name: stage-11-en
text: Above stand peaks that turn back the sun’s dragon chariot; below, rushing currents twist and surge. The paired directions, above and below, make height and danger felt in a single sweep of vision.

name: stage-12-en
text: How the Qingni road coils! A hundred steps, nine turns around the cliffs. The repeated turns exaggerate the road’s winding course. Each bend reveals a different relation between cliff, path and valley.

name: stage-13-en
text: Touching the stars, I look up with breath held; hand upon my chest, I sit and sigh. Reaching the constellations is an exaggeration of height. The held breath and long sigh bring that vastness back into the body.

name: stage-14-en
text: Sorrowful birds cry in ancient trees; one flies, its mate follows through the woods. Lift the lantern and follow the sound. Light reveals the near branches, while the distant valley remains quiet and dark.

name: stage-15-en
text: Again, a cuckoo calls beneath the moon; sorrow fills the empty mountain. Looking up changes the entire scene. The bird’s call carries human feeling into the mountain’s emptiness.

name: stage-16-en
text: Flying torrents and waterfalls roar; rocks thunder through ten thousand ravines. The verbs make water and stone feel forceful and alive. The quiet bird calls give way to the roar of the gorges.

name: stage-17-en
text: One man guards the pass; ten thousand cannot break through. The strategic mountain pass turns the poem from natural danger towards human affairs. The next lines ask what happens when its guardian cannot be trusted.

name: stage-18-en
text: Though the Brocade City offers pleasure, better to return home soon. Turn away from the fortress towards the valley. The poem’s advice to return carries concern for the traveller and anxiety about the world.

name: stage-19-en
text: Turning west, I sigh at length. The Hard Road to Shu does not end with a raised sail. We now return to Hard Is the Road, where remembered stories renew the hope of finding a way forward.

name: stage-20-en
text: At leisure I fish beside a jade-green stream. The image recalls Jiang Shang, who waited before receiving an opportunity to serve. The water grows quiet, but hope has not sunk beneath it.

name: stage-21-en
text: Then, in a dream, I sail beside the sun. The allusion to Yi Yin expresses the hope of being recognised. Here, dawn gives visible form to that hope.

name: stage-22-en
text: One day I shall ride the wind and cleave the waves, raise my cloud-high sail and cross the open sea. After hesitation, ice, snow and crossroads, the words one day express firm belief. The sail represents the will to go on.

name: stage-23-en
text: The mountains remain; the song continues. The sigh in The Hard Road to Shu and the sail in Hard Is the Road illuminate one another. Return to the original poems and listen to their different endings.

name: stage-0
text: 李太白邀君同游。诗吟蜀道之险峻，歌咏云海之壮丽。循一径山川，听千回心曲；从金樽前的迟疑，走向云帆下的曙光。

name: stage-2
text: 金樽清酒斗十千，玉盘珍羞直万钱。举樽，浅酌。轻轻放下，再尝一箸珍馐。席间的丰盛，终究留不住心中的安宁。

name: stage-3
text: 停杯投箸不能食。箸至半途，忽然停住。心事重重，难以下咽。放下，便不再举起。

name: stage-4
text: 拔剑四顾，心茫然。剑已出鞘，去路何方？

name: poem-xing-en
poem-shu-en
text:
Ah! How perilous, how high!
The road to Shu is harder than climbing to the blue sky.
Cancong and Yufu—how distant the founding of their kingdom!
For forty-eight thousand years it had no passage to the lands of Qin.
Westward, on Mount Taibai, only a bird’s path
could cross towards the heights of Mount Emei.
The earth split, mountains crumbled, and the strong men died;
only then were skyward stairs and cliff paths joined.
Above stand peaks that turn back the sun’s six-dragon chariot;
below, wild currents twist and surge.
Even the yellow crane cannot fly across;
apes and monkeys grieve at the climb.
How the Qingni road coils!
A hundred steps, nine turns around the cliffs.
Touching the stars of Shen and Jing, I look up with breath held;
hand upon my chest, I sit and sigh.

Traveller, when will you return from your western journey?
The perilous path and sheer cliffs cannot be climbed.
Only sorrowful birds cry in ancient trees;
one flies, its mate follows through the woods.
Again, a cuckoo calls beneath the moon—sorrow fills the empty mountain.
The road to Shu is harder than climbing to the blue sky;
hearing this can wither a youthful face.
Peak follows peak, less than a foot from heaven;
withered pines hang upside down from sheer rock walls.
Flying torrents and waterfalls compete in roaring;
water strikes cliffs and rolls stones, thundering through ten thousand ravines.
Such is the danger here!
You who have come so far—why have you come?

Sword Gate towers, sheer and formidable.
One man guards the pass; ten thousand cannot break through.
If the keeper is not loyal, he turns into a wolf or jackal.
At dawn beware of fierce tigers; at dusk beware of long snakes.
They bare their teeth and suck blood, killing people like cutting hemp.
Though the Brocade City offers pleasure, better to return home soon.
The road to Shu is harder than climbing to the blue sky;
turning west, I sigh at length.

name: cue-1-touch
text: 双手抵门。

name: cue-1-touch-en
text: Hands to the doors.

name: cue-1-open
text: 缓缓推开，入席听心。

name: cue-1-open-en
text: Push gently. Enter the light.

name: cue-2-cup
text: 举樽，浅酌，轻轻放下。

name: cue-2-cup-en
text: Raise the cup, sip, then lower it.

name: cue-2-taste
text: 取一箸珍馐，缓缓送近。

name: cue-2-taste-en
text: Lift a morsel. Bring it closer.

name: cue-2-swallow
text: 浅尝，咽下。

name: cue-2-swallow-en
text: Taste, and swallow.

name: cue-2-lower
text: 空箸退回，轻落案边。

name: cue-2-lower-en
text: Lower the empty chopsticks.

name: cue-3-hesitate
text: 欲食又止，箸停半途。

name: cue-3-hesitate-en
text: The hand hesitates.

name: cue-3-stop
text: 投箸落案，不能食。

name: cue-3-stop-en
text: I cannot eat.

name: cue-4-draw
text: 拔剑出鞘。

name: cue-4-draw-en
text: Draw the sword.

name: cue-4-gaze
text: 四顾茫茫，去路何方？

name: cue-4-gaze-en
text: Look all around. Where is the way?

name: cue-4-dark
text: 灯火渐远。

name: cue-4-dark-en
text: The lamplight fades.

name: cue-13-stars
text: 扪参历井，仰胁息。

name: cue-13-stars-en
text: Reach for the stars, breath held.

name: cue-13-sigh
text: 以手抚膺，坐长叹。

name: cue-13-sigh-en
text: Hand to the chest. A long sigh.

name: cue-14-light
text: 提灯，照见古木。

name: cue-14-light-en
text: Lift the lantern.

name: cue-14-distance
text: 循声远望，月照空山。

name: cue-14-distance-en
text: Look afar, into the moonlit valley.
